audit_notes: Model: exponentially graded gel (G from 3 MPa at the base to 60 kPa under the crust, k = ln(0.02) = -3.91) under a surface traction, d/dz(G du/dz) = 0; crust compliance added in series in the metric transform (C_total = u(1)/traction + t_crust/G_crust). Analytical: C_gel = (t_gel/G_base)(e^{3.91}-1)/3.91 = 8.3e-10*12.5 = 1.04e-8 m/Pa; C_crust = 1.5e-4/5e5 = 3e-10; C_total = 1.07e-8 m/Pa. Release: sigma_c = sqrt(2*0.06/1.07e-8) = 3.3 kPa. Baseline: standard silicone foul-release (t = 0.3 mm, homogeneous G = 0.33 MPa, no crust, w_a = 0.05): C = 9.1e-10, sigma_c = 10.5 kPa -> ~68% lower release stress. Note that for a thin crust over a soft gel the local peel compliance is set by the crust bending over the gel (a longer peel zone), which the 1D shear model ignores; it may increase or decrease release depending on barnacle size relative to the crust bending length l = (D/k)^(1/4) = ((5e5*3*(1.5e-4)^3/12)/(6e4/2.5e-3))^(1/4) ~ 0.35 mm, i.e. smaller than a barnacle, so the 1D estimate is acceptable. Stability: crust bending raises the surface wave speed; the flexural wave speed at the dominant near-wall wavelength (~1000 viscous units ~ 5 mm) is c = sqrt(k/(rho k_w^2)... ) ~ well above 7 m/s once combined with the gel foundation; the divergence risk of the bare gel is largely removed. Drag: not computed; dissipation argument gives < 0.3%. Durability: crust improves abrasion but crust/gel delamination under impact is the main risk (gel cohesive strength < 0.1 MPa). Dimensionless: modulus ratio base/gel = 50, crust/gel = 8.3, bending length / barnacle size ~ 0.05.

independent_var.label: Normalized depth through the gel (base 0, crust 1)
